Q1(a): Define Data Structure. Explain primitive and non-primitive data structures with classification diagram and memory allocation principles.

[Student Hand-Written Response]:
A data structure is a specialized format for organizing, processing, retrieving, and storing data in computer memory efficiently.
• Primitive Data Structures: Int (4 bytes), Float (4 bytes), Char (1 byte), Double (8 bytes), Pointer.
• Non-Primitive Data Structures:
  - Linear: Arrays, Stacks, Queues, Linked Lists (sequential layout).
  - Non-Linear: Trees, Graphs (hierarchical layout).
• Memory Allocation: Static allocation uses stack memory at compile-time. Dynamic allocation uses heap memory at runtime via pointers.

Q1(b): Explain Knuth-Morris-Pratt (KMP) pattern matching algorithm. Trace failure function π for P = "ababaca".

[Student Hand-Written Response]:
KMP algorithm avoids backtracking text pointer i by computing prefix function π (failure function) on pattern P.
Failure function π for P = "ababaca":
• Index: 1 2 3 4 5 6 7
• Char:  a b a b a c a
• π val: 0 0 1 2 3 0 1
Time Complexity: O(n + m) linear matching time compared to O(n*m) naive algorithm.

Q2(a): Explain dynamic memory allocation functions in C: malloc(), calloc(), realloc(), free().

[Student Hand-Written Response]:
• malloc(size_t size): Allocates uninitialized memory on heap. Returns void* or NULL.
• calloc(num, size): Allocates zero-initialized contiguous memory.
• realloc(ptr, new_size): Resizes existing block.
• free(ptr): Deallocates memory block to prevent memory leaks.
